Kannan, aged about 42 years, vide detention order dated 30-6-2025 on the file of the 2nd respondent herein made in the proceedings in detention order C.M.P. judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Sunder Mohan, J.:— The petitioner, who is the mother of detenu Dhatchinamoorthy, S/o. Kannan, branded as Goonda under Section 2(f) of the Tamil Nadu Preventive Detention Act, 1982 (Tamil Nadu Act 14 of 1982) (in short “Act”) has challenged his detention order dated 30-6-2025.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the detention order is liable to be quashed on the ground that there is a delay in passing the order of detention and that the subjective satisfaction of the detaining authority in arriving at the conclusion that the detenu is likely to be released on bail by relying upon the order passed by this Court, suffers from non-application of mind.

3. Heard the learned Additional Public Prosecutor.

4. In this case, the detenu was arrested on 30-5-2025 and detained on 30-6-2025. The facts of the Sushanta Kumar Banik v. State of Tripura, reported in “2022 LiveLaw (SC) 813” would squarely apply to the facts of the instant case as the live and proximate link between the ground of detention and the purpose of detention stood snapped.

5. Secondly, we find that the detaining authority has relied upon an order passed in Crl.OP No. 8576 of 2025 to conclude that the detenu is likely to be released on bail. The facts in the order relied upon by the detaining authority are not similar to the facts of the instant case. In that case, the accused had one previous case whereas in this case, the accused has two previous cases. Further in this case, the detenu had been charged for the offences under Section 111(2)(b) and Section 123 of BNS, 2023 whereas in the case relied upon by the detaining authority, accused had been charged for offence under Section 123 of BNS, 2023. Therefore, we are of the view that the order of the detaining authority suffers from non-application of mind and is liable to be set aside.

6. In light of the above discussion, this Habeas Corpus Petition is allowed and the Detention Order passed by the second respondent in C.M.P. No. 32/Goonda/Salem City/2025, dated 30-6-2025 is hereby set aside.

7. The detenu viz. Dhatchinamoorthy, S/o. Kannan, aged 23 years, who is now confined in Central Prison, Salem, is hereby directed to be set at liberty forthwith unless his presence is required in connection with any other case.
